messages.subject: recruitment rate and area increase
parts:
Hi all

I have ocelot (Leopardus pardalis) data from seven systematic camera trap surveys. These surveys were realized in 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2014, 2016 and 2018. I am fitting openCR, using JSSAsecrlCL model type, and also JSSAsecrfCL model type.

The sampled site was always the same, but in each survey the surface was increased, incorporating new areas.

My question is, can the recruitment rate estimate be biased by the increase in area?

Many thanks

Paula

messages.author: e14baef37a11434f
messages.subject: Re: recruitment rate and area increase
parts:
According to my understanding of open spatial models, the recruitment rate should be unbiased as area increases provided that 1) the actual recruitment rate isn’t different in these new areas you’re expanding into, 2) detection, movement, sex ratio, etc is similar in these expanded areas to your core, and 3) assuming you’ve done the general analysis right (wide enough buffer etc).

Best regards,
Clayton

Many thanks for your response.

The whole area is similar in landscape and human access conditions, so it is expected all demographic parameters to be similar. Buffer mask it is also wide.

Your answer makes sense with the results I got. I modeled the recruitment rate by sessions, and by sex, and the estimation was always the same.

Thanks!

Best

paula
